Report_ID: Proportion of patients with at least one asthma exacerbation (any reported exacerbation)
Title: Superiority of fluticasone propionate/formoterol fumarate versus fluticasone propionate alone in patients with moderate-to-severe asthma: a randomised controlled trial
Author: Pertseva et al.
Comment: The reported participant counts cover any asthma exacerbation, not specifically moderate-to-severe exacerbations. Methods define mild–moderate exacerbations to include PEFR reduction, nocturnal awakening, or increased rescue-albuterol use; severe exacerbations require additional therapy such as systemic steroids, an emergency visit, or hospitalisation. Thus this is broader than the planned outcome and should not be treated as an exact moderate-to-severe count. The paper-reported odds ratio is oriented as SKP FP relative to fluticasone/formoterol; no risk ratio was reported, so RR fields are left null.; group_1/group_2 fields swapped: the extractor itself stated group_1_label ('Fluticasone/formoterol 250/10 μg b.i.d.') is the intervention arm (group_1_is_control=False); excluded by outcome classification: does not match the requested outcome/timepoint (meta_analysis_candidate=False)
Design Type: Double-blind randomised active-controlled parallel-group multicentre trial
Study Environment: Primary care clinics and hospital clinics at 68 sites
Country: Europe, South America and the United States
Topic of Content: Moderate-to-severe asthma uncontrolled on prior inhaled corticosteroid therapy
Participant type: Adolescents and adults aged 12 years and older with moderate-to-severe symptomatic asthma and prior ICS use
Recruitment source: Primary care clinics and hospital clinics
Outcome measurement: Patients with at least one asthma exacerbation during the randomised treatment period
Outcome variable: Proportion of patients with at least one asthma exacerbation (any reported exacerbation)

Title: Efficacy of budesonide/formoterol pressurized metered-dose inhaler versus budesonide pressurized metered-dose inhaler alone in Hispanic adults and adolescents with asthma: a randomized, controlled trial
Author: Zangrilli et al.
Comment: The paper does not report the planned composite of participants with at least one moderate or severe exacerbation. This row captures only a serious adverse event labeled 'status asthmaticus' and may omit other qualifying exacerbations. The paper does not explicitly state that this event required systemic corticosteroids, an emergency visit, or hospitalization, although it appears under serious adverse events. Use in the primary meta-analysis only if the review protocol accepts this as the closest available severe-exacerbation definition. Title: Fluticasone Furoate–Vilanterol 100-25 mcg Compared with Fluticasone Furoate 100 mcg in Asthma: A Randomized Trial
Author: Bleecker et al.
Comment: The enrolled population included patients previously receiving low-to-medium-dose ICS or low-dose ICS-LABA, so it was not restricted to uncontrolled medium-dose ICS users. Only severe exacerbations were reported, not the planned combined moderate-or-severe outcome. Denominators are the ITT population, defined as randomized participants who received at least one dose. The paper did not report an FF-VI-versus-FF risk ratio, so RR fields are left null.
